summary: the cases of tests/run fatwrite under etude, against a FAT32 driver that never sets the dirty flag, one that writes every FAT entry of a run through on its own, and one that leaves a removed file's clusters allocated

argv: sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 && sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel

faults.name: never-dirty
faults.summary: the first metadata change of a mount clears the dirty flag instead of setting it, so that a machine ended in the middle of a write leaves a volume that says it was unmounted cleanly

faults.name: entry-through
faults.summary: every FAT entry is written through on its own, even in a batch, so that a large write and its removal take a disk command for each cluster

faults.name: chain-kept
faults.summary: a removed file's cluster chain is never freed, so that the host's walk finds clusters allocated and reached by nothing
